exercises.title: The Architecture of Biophilic Urban Design
exercises.title_uz: Biofil shahar arxitekturasi va uning psixologik ta’siri
exercises.description_uz: IELTS Academic Reading Passage 2 standarti. True/False/Not Given va xulosa to‘ldirish savollari.
exercises.passage_or_prompt:
For decades, modern metropolitan landscapes have been dominated by steel, concrete, and asphalt—materials engineered for structural efficiency and density rather than biological harmony. However, an emerging architectural paradigm known as 'biophilic design' posits that human psychological and physiological equilibrium is intrinsically intertwined with natural ecosystems. Pioneered by sociobiologist Edward O. Wilson, the biophilia hypothesis suggests that humans possess an innate biological affinity for the living world.

Recent empirical investigations conducted in Singapore and Copenhagen indicate that integrating vertical forests, sky gardens, and uninhibited natural light into high-density commercial towers correlates with a 15% reduction in occupational stress and a measurable improvement in cognitive restoration. Architects argue that this approach transcends mere aesthetic embellishment; it fundamentally redesigns environmental acoustics and improves interior air filtration through natural evapotranspiration.

Nonetheless, skeptics contend that biophilic retrofitting presents steep economic barriers. The structural reinforcement needed to support elevated soil loads and irrigation systems elevates upfront engineering costs by approximately 18 to 22 percent. Moreover, without rigorous botanical management, non-native plant species introduce pest liabilities. Despite these fiscal hurdles, leading municipal authorities in Tokyo and Melbourne are now codifying mandatory living-wall ratios for new commercial developments, asserting that the long-term public health savings far outweigh initial capital expenditures.

exercises.title: The Cognitive Architecture of Bilingualism
exercises.title_uz: Ikki tillilikning kognitiv arxitekturasi va xotira mustahkamligi
exercises.description_uz: IELTS Academic Reading standarti. 5 ta paragraf. Fokusli o‘chib borish va dalillar tahlili.
exercises.passage_or_prompt:
For over a century, psycholinguists and educators maintained that learning two languages concurrently during childhood produced cognitive friction. Early 20th-century assessments routinely concluded that bilingual youngsters suffered from diminished vocabulary acquisition and linguistic hesitation. However, modern neuroimaging technologies, including functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI), have thoroughly dismantled this outdated paradigm, demonstrating that managing two active linguistic systems yields profound neural advantages.

At the epicenter of this cognitive enhancement is the brain's executive control system—a distributed neural network housed within the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Whenever a bilingual individual speaks, both language systems remain activated simultaneously. The brain must constantly suppress the non-target language while retrieving words from the target language. This continuous mental workout strengthens neural pathways responsible for attentional control, cognitive flexibility, and task switching.

Empirical investigations orchestrated by cognitive neuroscientist Dr. Ellen Bialystok revealed that bilingual individuals systematically outperform monolinguals in complex problem-solving scenarios that involve conflicting perceptual cues. In the celebrated Simon and Flanker tests, bilingual participants demonstrated significantly faster reaction latencies and reduced susceptibility to distracting visual stimuli, proving their heightened ability to filter extraneous noise.

Beyond immediate executive function benefits, sustained bilingualism appears to construct a formidable biological safeguard against neurodegenerative disorders. Clinical studies across North America and Europe found that lifelong bilingual patients diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease manifest clinical symptoms of cognitive decline four to five years later than their monolingual counterparts with equivalent levels of brain pathology. Neuroscientists attribute this phenomenon to 'cognitive reserve'—an enhanced capacity of the brain to compensate for structural degradation through alternative neural routes.

Nevertheless, linguistic scholars emphasize that these cognitive dividends are not accrued instantaneously through superficial language exposure. The neurological benefits correlate directly with the depth of linguistic immersion, regular switching between languages, and communicative intensity. As globalized societies increasingly recognize the clinical and computational value of neuroplasticity, promoting early bilingual education is emerging as a cornerstone of modern cognitive public policy.

exercises.title: Campus Accommodation and Student Support Briefing
exercises.title_uz: Universitet yotoqxonasi va talabalar markazi brifingi
exercises.description_uz: IELTS Listening Section 1 & 2 formati. Telefon orqali ro‘yxatdan o‘tish va qoidalar.
exercises.passage_or_prompt: Listen to the conversation between an international student and an accommodation coordinator.
exercises.audio_transcript:
Officer: Good morning, University Housing Office. How may I help you?
Student: Hello. I'm an incoming postgraduate student from Uzbekistan. My name is Dilshod Rakhimov. I'd like to confirm my residence hall allocation.
Officer: Welcome Dilshod! Let me pull up your student portal. Could you provide your student ID number?
Student: Yes, it is UK-90842.
Officer: Thank you. Yes, you have been assigned to 'Meadow View Hall', Room 402B. It includes an en-suite bathroom and shared kitchen facilities with 4 other postgrads.
Student: That sounds excellent. What is the quarterly rental fee, and does it include broadband internet?
Officer: The quarterly rent is 1,850 pounds, fully inclusive of ultra-fast fiber broadband, heating, and water. Laundry cards can be loaded online.
Student: Perfect. What is the latest check-in time on September 18th?
Officer: The reception desk operates 24 hours, but key collection for inventory inspection must be completed before 8:00 PM.

exercises.title: IELTS Academic Writing Task 2: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education
exercises.title_uz: Writing Task 2: Ta’limda sun’iy intellektning roli
exercises.description_uz: 250 ta so‘zdan kam bo‘lmagan to‘liq akademik insho yozing. 40 daqiqa vaqt ajratilgan.
exercises.passage_or_prompt:
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.

Write about the following topic:

"Some people believe that artificial intelligence tools will entirely replace human university professors within the next two decades, while others maintain that human mentorship remains irreplaceable in higher education."

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

exercises.title: Manchester Central Library Orientation & Digital Archives
exercises.title_uz: Shahar markaziy kutubxonasi va arxivlar bo‘yicha qo‘llanma
exercises.description_uz: IELTS Listening Section 2 formati. Monolog tinglash, qoidalar va xonalar taqsimoti.
exercises.passage_or_prompt: Listen to the chief archivist delivering an orientation talk to new university researchers.
exercises.audio_transcript:
Speaker: Good morning and welcome to Manchester Central Library. My name is Helen Davies, the chief archivist, and today I will give you a quick orientation before you start your research projects.
First of all, our opening hours are Monday to Saturday from 8:30 AM to 7:00 PM. On Sundays, we are open strictly between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM for private study only.
Now, regarding the floor layout. As you enter through the main revolving doors on the Ground Floor, you will see the Reception Desk straight ahead. If you turn immediately to your left, you will find the New Arrivals and Fiction wing. To your right is the Computer and Internet Lab, which has 40 workstations.
The Second Floor houses our Humanities and Social Sciences collections, alongside our Group Study Pods. Please remember, group discussions are strictly confined to these pods.
For those of you conducting historical or genealogical research, the Rare Manuscripts and Local Heritage Archives are located on Level 3. Access to this level requires a pre-booked security badge, which you can obtain from Reception after paying a refundable key deposit of 20 pounds.
Lastly, standard members can borrow up to 8 books at any time for a duration of 3 weeks. Fines for overdue books are 50 pence per day, so please renew them online through your library account.
Now, if you have any questions, I will be glad to take them.

exercises.title: Marine Bioluminescence: Biological Mechanisms & Evolutionary Functions
exercises.description_uz: IELTS Listening Section 4 formati. Monolog akademik ma’ruza, kimyoviy jarayonlar va funksiyalar.
exercises.passage_or_prompt: Listen to part of an academic lecture on marine biology.
exercises.audio_transcript:
Lecturer: Good afternoon, students. In today's marine biology lecture, we will examine bioluminescence — the production and emission of light by living organisms in aquatic environments.
Unlike incandescent light bulbs, which lose over 90 percent of their energy as heat, bioluminescent light is known as cold light. In fact, less than 20 percent of the reaction produces thermal energy, making it exceptionally efficient.
The fundamental chemical reaction requires two unique compounds: a light-emitting pigment called luciferin, and an enzyme known as luciferase. When luciferin reacts with oxygen in the presence of luciferase, light is produced.
Now, why have deep-sea creatures developed this capability? Marine biologists categorize its evolutionary functions into three main purposes.
First, offensive predation. The anglerfish famously dangles a luminous lure from its head, mimicking small prey to attract unsuspecting fish into its jaws.
Second, defensive camouflage. Many squid and fish species employ a technique called counter-illumination. By emitting faint bluish light from their ventral underbellies, they match the sunlight filtering down from the surface, effectively rendering themselves invisible to predators lurking beneath them.
And third, intraspecific communication and mating displays, frequently observed in ostracod crustaceans off the Caribbean reefs.
Tomorrow, we will explore laboratory applications of GFP, or green fluorescent protein, derived from jellyfish.

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor that increases the initial cost of biophilic buildings by up to 22%?
options: A) Importing rare exotic flowers from South America
B) Structural reinforcement for soil loads and irrigation systems
C) High salaries required by European botanical specialists
D) Acoustic monitoring sensors placed throughout the ceiling
questions.correct_answer: B) Structural reinforcement for soil loads and irrigation systems
questions.explanation_uz: Matnda xarajat 18-22% oshishi sababi sifatida tuproq og‘irligi va sug‘orish tizimlari uchun muhandislik mustahkamlashi ko‘rsatilgan.
questions.evidence_passage: The structural reinforcement needed to support elevated soil loads and irrigation systems elevates upfront engineering costs by approximately 18 to 22 percent.

questions.question_text: Early 20th-century researchers believed that raising children bilingually enhanced their vocabulary growth.

questions.evidence_passage: Early 20th-century assessments routinely concluded that bilingual youngsters suffered from diminished vocabulary acquisition and linguistic hesitation.

questions.question_text: Both languages remain active in a bilingual brain even when only one language is being spoken.

questions.evidence_passage: Whenever a bilingual individual speaks, both language systems remain activated simultaneously.

questions.question_text: Why is bioluminescent light described as 'cold light'?
options: It only occurs in freezing polar ocean depths
Less than 20% of the reaction produces thermal energy
It requires temperatures below zero to activate
It completely absorbs heat from surrounding seawater
questions.correct_answer: Less than 20% of the reaction produces thermal energy
questions.explanation_uz: Ma'ruzachi reaksiyaning 20% dan kamrog'i issiqlik energiyasi hosil qilishini, shuning uchun 'sovuq nur' deb atalishini tushuntiradi.
questions.evidence_passage: In fact, less than 20 percent of the reaction produces thermal energy, making it exceptionally efficient.

questions.question_text: What two compounds are essential for producing bioluminescent light?
questions.explanation_uz: Reaksiya lyutsiferin (pigment) va lyutsiferaza (ferment) birikmasini talab qiladi.
questions.evidence_passage: ...a light-emitting pigment called luciferin, and an enzyme known as luciferase.

questions.question_text: How does 'counter-illumination' protect marine species from predators?
options: It temporarily blinds approaching predators with flashes
It produces heat shock waves in the water
It matches surface light to conceal their silhouette from beneath

questions.explanation_uz: Qorindagi yorug'lik tepadan tushayotgan quyosh nuri bilan uyg'unlashib, pastdagi yirtqichlarga ko'rinmas qiladi.
